title: Why MLX — Prince Canuma, Neywa Labs
talk_summary: A demo-driven advocacy talk for MLX, Apple's array framework for running vision, audio, and LLM inference on-device on Apple silicon, with community examples (real-time detection, TTS, robotics). It contains almost no agent-orchestration or review-quality content; the only transferable mechanisms are KV-cache quantization (TurboQuant) and modular pipeline composition.

takeaways.what_they_do: Quantizes the KV cache to shrink memory and raise throughput at long context, claiming near-identical output quality to the full-precision model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the full model takes uh almost 1 GB of uh KV cache or RAM and by using Turbo Quant you can reduce that by 4x
takeaways.numbers: ~4x KV-cache memory reduction; ~2x throughput at ~300k context

takeaways.what_they_do: Composes pipelines from independently chosen components (ASR model, LLM, TTS) so each stage can be swapped to fit a hardware/cost budget.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can choose which language model you want, and you can also choose which text-to-speech model you want
